Start with a tutorial to complete one calculation. Use the task guides when you adapt that calculation to your own circuit, and the references when you need exact argument or output rules.

## Reader paths

| You want to… | Start here |
|---|---|
| Install the package and public component library | [Install SCGSim](course/installation.qmd) |
| Build the model used by the beginner tutorials | [SimplePad model](tutorials/simplepad-model.qmd) |
| Compute capacitance | [Prepare](tutorials/capacitance/prepare.qmd) → [Run](tutorials/capacitance/run.qmd) → [Analyze](tutorials/capacitance/analyze.qmd) |
| Compute resonance and EPR | [Prepare](tutorials/resonance-epr/prepare.qmd) → [Run](tutorials/resonance-epr/run.qmd) → [Analyze](tutorials/resonance-epr/analyze.qmd) |
| Adapt a model, run a solver or read results | [Tutorial and task index](examples.qmd) |
| Look up supported inputs and outputs | [Reference topics](reference.qmd) |
| Contribute code or documentation | [Contributing](contributing.qmd) |

## Source ownership

SCGSim documentation explains its geometry, preparation, execution and result APIs. [OrcaPen SC PDK](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk) owns public components, process stacks and executable component notebooks. Links to a particular example retain that example's source revision; its installation recipe belongs in the [installation guide](course/installation.qmd#example-environments).

When changing a linked OrcaPen example, check the SCGSim pages that link to it. When changing a SCGSim API, check both the task guide and the corresponding example. Keep the notebook's canonical source in the PDK repository.
